chunks: Say: "If what you wish to be hastened were in my power, all matters between you and me would have been settled; God is cognisant of those who are unjust."
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'If what you wish to be hastened were in my power' in Surah Al-An'am?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-An'am, this verse highlights the Prophet's (SAWW) role as a mere conveyer of divine will, distinguishing his human limitation from God's absolute authority over the timing of judgment. Shia exegesis often links this to the concept of *Tawhid al-Af'al*, emphasizing that while the Prophet possesses deep knowledge, the actual execution of divine decrees remains exclusively with Allah, who best knows the true state of the unjust.
